subject: Dedicated capacity proposal — request for migration credits and competitive match
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@cloudscale.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cloudscale.com, Mark Jensen <mjensen@cloudscale.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated GPU pool sizing + pricing (RFP follow-up)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the call yesterday. We're wrapping up the internal RFP review and want to confirm a few items before we move to legal:

- Target GPU pool: 24 A100-equivalent GPUs (steady-state), ability to burst to 36 for training windows.
- Throughput target: ~120 qps sustained across text-gen workloads (avg seq length ~512).
- Commit: 12-month reserved capacity (start-of-term).

We received pricing from another vendor that includes an onboarding credit to offset migration and re-architecting (~$200k). Your term sheet (v3) looks clean but the list price is ~12% higher than their committed quote.

Can you advise on whether Redwood can offer a migration credit or match their committed discount? If not, what alternative packaging/guarantees can we get to make the economics comparable (e.g., guaranteed throughput SLA, free training window bursts, or flexible scaling credits)?

I've attached the RFP excerpt and our internal cost model.

Thanks,
Elena
Sr. Cloud Infrastructure, CloudScale

Attachments: CloudScale-RFP.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool sizing + pricing (RFP follow-up)

Elena —

Appreciate the detail and for sharing the RFP. Quick initial thoughts:

- We can meet the 24 GPU steady-state with burst-to-36 behavior using our Dedicated pool + autoscale policy. We'll include a 2-hour guaranteed burst window per day for free during the first 3 months to support initial training migrations.
- Throughput: based on your seq lengths, we can guarantee 110 qps P95 with our baseline config; to reach 120 qps we'd recommend a modest I/O optimization and a quantization profile — happy to include that in onboarding.
- Pricing: attached is Redwood-Dedicated-Term-Sheet-v3 with a 15% volume discount at the proposed commit level.

Regarding migration credit: we don't typically provide a flat credit at the list level, but we can consider a one-time onboarding credit or a blended discount if there's an accelerated signing commitment.

Options I can propose to make pricing competitive:
- Option A: $100k onboarding credit + 15% discount on committed capacity (standard).
- Option B: $0 onboarding credit + 18% discount if you commit to a 24-month reserved term.
- Option C: $150k onboarding credit + 15% discount + guaranteed 2-hour daily burst for 6 months (requires exec sign-off).

If you can share the competitor quote (high level), I can try to take Option C up for internal approval.

Regards,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood-Dedicated-Term-Sheet-v3.pdf
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@cloudscale.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cloudscale.com, Mark Jensen <mjensen@cloudscale.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool sizing + pricing (RFP follow-up)

Karthik,

Thanks — that helps. High level on the competitor offer: 18% discount + $200k one-time migration credit if signed within 10 business days. They also included a 99.9% throughput SLA and a clause for a single 30-day trial window that doesn't count against commit.

CloudScale prefers to stay with Redwood if the economics are similar — main ask is the $200k migration credit or a combination of credit + enhanced SLA that brings our TCO in line. Option C looks closest. Can you push that up for exec approval?

Also important: procurement will need a DocuSign-ready term sheet with the final concession spelled out.

Best,
Elena
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated GPU pool sizing + pricing — escalation for exec credit approval

Team — looping you in because CloudScale is asking for a $200k migration credit (or equivalent mix) and an SLA match (99.9% throughput). They are comparing a competing committed offer tied to an accelerated signature window.

Key deal facts:
- ARR-equivalent at commit: ~$1.8M for 12 months on 24-GPU reserved pool.
- Upside: additional managed services + potential expansion to EU region next year.
- Asks: $200k migration credit OR Option C ($150k credit + 15% disc + 2-hour burst x 6 months).

I'm requesting exec approval to offer Option C but want guidance on whether we can stretch to $200k (if so, require one additional concession: 18-month contract or prepay). Legal will need to update the term sheet and procurement wants a DocuSign link.

Can you advise quickly? Elena indicated they need the DocuSign-ready concession within 48 hours to stay in their accelerated window.

— Karthik
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 19 Sep 2027 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated GPU pool sizing + pricing — escalation for exec credit approval

Karthik — thanks for the context. I'm comfortable approving a deal-level concession with these guardrails:

- One-time migration credit up to $125,000.
- Add a free onboarding month (invoice credit equal to one month of committed spend) to bridge the delta vs. competitor.
- Require an 18-month commit OR full prepay for 12 months to unlock the full credit.
- Include a targeted SLA bump to 99.85% for throughput with a service credit structure (not full penalty exposure).

Operational asks: have Legal draft an addendum that spells out the credit timing, the trial/burst windows, and the SLA measurement. Finance to sign off on revenue recognition. This keeps the net present value acceptable while giving CloudScale near-competitive economics.

If CloudScale insists on $200k flat credit, we should ask for a 24-month commit and escalated discounting — not ideal. Push Option C with our approved $125k + 1 month onboarding free.

Ben
VP, Sales Operations
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, procurement@cloudscale.com
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool sizing + pricing (RFP follow-up) — updated concession

Elena —

Thanks for your patience. Per internal review we can offer the following concession to get you to parity with the competitor while keeping our economic guardrails in place:

Final offer (requires signature on addendum within 10 business days):
- One-time migration credit: $125,000 applied as invoice credit at start-of-term.
- One month of committed spend waived (applied as onboarding credit).
- 15% committed discount on the 12-month reserved pool.
- 2-hour guaranteed daily burst for 6 months (to support training windows).
- SLA: 99.85% throughput P95 with service credit structure; measurement details in addendum.

Condition: either an 18-month commit or full prepay for 12 months will unlock the full $125k credit. If you prefer 12-month prepay, Finance will provide the invoice schedule.

I've asked Legal to prepare a DocuSign-ready addendum (link to follow). If you can confirm acceptance of the conditions by end of week, we'll prioritize the signature path.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood-Dedicated-Term-Sheet-v3.pdf
Links: https://www.docusign.com/DocuSignLink/ABC123
